reviews.review: [spoiler] I HATE BAD ENDINGS T.T [/spoiler]
holy what a game one of the if not the best narrative i have ever played 100% recomend
I have no words. I really good game
Absolute ride of a game.

I initially got this game because it gave me Case of The Golden Idol vibes, but got something different entirely. Now, this is by no means a bad thing. On the contrary, I loved my time with this game. It drew me in within the first hour, and I stayed until I had beaten the entire thing in one sitting. I was slapped in the face with one of the biggest plot twists of all time. I will probably remember this one for a long time coming for being so well polished and well thought out.

Do not expect this to be a simulation style game. It is a story game. That said, it is very interesting and I'm having fun with it, it does make you feel intelligent if you figure things out without help.
Good game. Don’t consider. Buy it and play.
pretty fun. not too challenging. kind of a cheesy twist.
wow
Please just take 3 hours to play this. You will be changed on the other side.
Fun and story rich little gem of a game. You can't save and backtrack however so make sure your decisions are valid or risk replaying it to get more content.

Great game. X-files by way of Hacknet. Sort of. 

It's very linear, there's not a ton of "choices matter" stuff here, but it the narrative is compelling, and it's got REALLY good atmosphere and vibes. 

My only real gripe with it is that the story doesn't really feel like it reaches a conclusion, more that it hit a dead end. It ties many of its loose ends up, but in a very boring way. But the journey... Whew, boy, the journey makes it totally worth it.

Took me about 2.7 hours to complete, but that's after continuing my save from the demo, the time played from which I assume did not carry over.

For $12-15 you could do much, much worse.
i dont even have the words to properly praise this game. holy $hit.
It's short, it's expensive, it's high production, it's worth the ride. This is an interactive movie, treat it like one. Get some popcorn, 3-4 hours, and enjoy.

I love this game!!!
I highly recommend

Took me roughly 4ish hours to get through this, but man, it was a really cool 4 hours.

You play the role as an "Operator" supporting the "FDI" supporting Agents in the field. As the story moves on, there's more than meets the eye and you find yourself in the heart of a conspiracy. Won't say much more there as I don't want to ruin anything, but the twist reveal is perfect. It gives you just enough evidence to figure it out to where the lightbulb kicks on, then the big reveal.

Game is super immersive, great puzzles (with built in hints if you get stuck), awesome story, and top notch production value.

Once I started playing, I was hooked and couldn't put it down until it was finished. If you like immersive, story driven puzzle games, I cannot recommend this enough. It's a really cool ride.

I normally don't ever leave reviews but this game is a masterpiece. Go in completely blind, it'll suck you in for a few hours. Insane plot, great sound design, and super cool little puzzles. Highly recommend!
Short, simple but absolutely amazing game. The story has just the right amount of hints to keep you going, and a twist at the end (that some may see coming)

Its a good play through story game but I'm a bit disappointed in that it doesn't just have dynamic puzzles and things to solve like papers please or other games like this. It has all the base level mechanics for that but its just a play through game that is very linear... Played a few times trying to get different endings only to do the same thing every time... Even the bomb defusing part was exactly the same... Hopefully they expand and create dynamic cases that you just have to solve and not play the "story mode"... I've spent more for less no doubt but I was expecting more for this much...
This game is really good, I would recommend !

Once I saw the trailer, I wishlisted the game. And once it was released, I bought it as soon as possible. This game is a new kind of game, and that's what I like about it. It's something new. The soundtrack is brilliant, amazing, and the voice acting, the colors. The only thing I didn't like was that the cases don't look good. I didn't like that the cases are somehow connected and it's kind of difficult. I got stuck in some parts for more than an hour.

fun game.

Absolutely excellent. A very well written and gripping narrative experience in a very Xfiles-esque mould. I do wish this was a tad longer, but its only a minor gripe and its amazing regardless. Hopefully we get more from this team at some point, Im looking forwards to their next project.

ABSOLUTELY PHENOMENAL CHANGED MY LIFE SEQUEL PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE AND OH MY GOD THE SOUND DESIGN ?????? absolutely cracked

apart from early game bugs that cause it to crash several times, this game has a strong story line. As far as game play, my only objection is  your choices don't always matter. I tried to play this game a certain way but it doesn't seem to make a difference so far and forces you down a certain path. At this point however I can't get past the game breaking bugs. currently (as of first day release) this game crashes my computer ever 15 minutes and after 3 hours of play my save file just disappeared causing me to have to restart.
Im not gonna lie, im one hour in and i can say this is one of the coolest game i have played in YEARS. im tense all the time. SO FUCKING COOL. if you reading this, dont search for spoilers.

HOLY SHIT THIS GAME MAKES ME WANT TO WORK FOR THE FBI. The jumpscares always get me shitting my pants but the attention to detail is fucking awesome. 10/10 would recommend even though I lack the balls to finish this damn game.

I played the game full and through my first time opening it. It is beautiful and different, the music, the suspense, the gameplay all amazing and beautiful. I wish I had more and I hope to see more games like this. By far one of my favorite games ever played.

A gripping conspiracy story, played almost entirely through interacting with a computer terminal. The sound design and soundtrack are great, the interface feels nice. Overall, I very much enjoyed the atmosphere. Most of the time, you're looking for clues much in the style of highlighting policy violations in Papers, Please. While the game doesn't offer much mechanically, the plot is short enough that it never becomes boring – it takes its time to tell its story, but no more than that.

TL;DR: This game is a 3-hour long visual novel with not-that-meaningful choices, good music and sound effects, narration, and an interesting but short linear story line. 0 replay-ability.

The nice things:

[spoiler]1. The cutscenes where the game shows you that time has passed is nice. The subtle drug-taking noises and coughing noises makes a good addition. Even though there is no real graphics here, it shows that the developers put in a lot of efforts in making the game immersive.
2. The interface and UI, especially the keyboard noises you make when you are typing, makes me reminiscent of a time when I wasn't even alive. It just feels nice to type things and click on things.
3. Narration is good, not crazy impressive, but good. That's a hard bar to pass by my standards.
4. Mechanics are nice, problem solving feels rewarding, visual and audio clues are subtle yet noticeable.[/spoiler]

The first playthrough of the game is amazing, but there are a few nick-picking things.

[spoiler]1. Agents not reacting differently when you call them by their first names instead of their last names.
2. During the first interaction with HAL, I chose to report her to my supervisor. And after the second one, I ratted her out again because I felt even if she helped me she is still wanted for good reasons. Even when I ratted her out twice, she still choose to help me with mellow tones and such. I'd expect some type of pissed-off-but-still-have-to-work-with-you type of attitude. (This can be explained with later plots but, a pissed-off reaction would've been nice, it would feel like the game recognized my choices.)
3. During the agent Andrews infiltration event, the security camera added immersion but served little to no purpose. She could complete her task no matter what, and even though we spotted for her to avoid the walking personnel, it didn't seem to matter because the guy didn't do anything when he literally saw her in the first pass.
4. I just finished my second playthrough, this game has 0 replay-ability. Everything is the same, your choices don't matter where the story goes, Tanner will always die in the end. I guess its building for a potential sequal.
5. The game teased the true identity of the Mike waaaaaay too easy. As the head of the entire secret service unit, you would go ahead and call 'your friend' during work through secured line just chatting? Also, he lied about having a wife while his files show that he is single. Meanwhile the game constantly push how weird Skinner is but they exposed the lead on Mike way too early and way too easily.[/spoiler]

Finally, if you have finished the game.
[spoiler]Can anyone tell me what 25000100193555 means? This code is written in the ALICE file in your trashbin if you open the folder before HAL gives you the code. If you open it again after HAL gives you the code it updates to the usual letter from Alice. The code doesn't open any files in the HDD, I wonder what its used for, its the only remaining mystery in this game for me.[/spoiler]
Very good story short but good.
Loved this. One of the best interactive / puzzle games I have ever played. Wish there were more games like this.

Great little story game. Can't wait for more [spoiler] especially if there's a continuation [/spoiler] . Well worth the cost even if a few of the mechanics are only used once. It made me want for more of the base gameplay so if anyone knows of more like this let me know! Only thing I would suggest probably would be being able to skip forward in dialog/cutscenes might be nice for going after achieves
Excellent writing. Excellent game.
It was a nice short game. Looking forward to more from this developer.
This game has a fantastic story and it'll be one that sticks with me for a very long time. Play it for yourself and try not to spoil it for the best experience!

For $20 CAD this has got to be one of the best story games the final plot twist had me staring at the screen with my jaw dropped, great story. I only wish that they release another game maybe a part 2 as id love to see where the story goes further. 10/10 all day.

I never leave reviews, but I tried this game's demo, and I was instantly hooked.  I love a good detective puzzler, especially ones based around federal bureaus.  The demo hooked me, and I immediately decided to buy this game day one, which is unusual for me, since I also don't usually buy games day one.

The story is amazing, but I feel like I messed up somewhere and ended up with the bad ending.  Going to have to play it again later this week and see if I can get a good ending....
The game is a bit short and the cliffhanger ending is a bit disappointing. I did enjoy it while it lasts.
Short, very immersive, excellent game.

Fantastic fun game, voice acting, music, the setting of the game its great. 100% recommended

10/10. The game does a very good job of giving you lots of clues that keep being relevant. As you learn more and more information, those old clues start to make more and more sense. The puzzle pieces are all there, its just up to you to put it all together.

Amazing game for an evening playthrough with 2,5 - 4 hour playtime. Entertaining story with a few twists and turns that surprised me. No bugs at all. 100% can recommend for anyone who likes light detective work and a good story.

If you've played games like Orwell or Hacknet, this is pretty much a great combination of both. Amazing play style, very interesting riddles to go through, soundtrack that fits the game perfectly. I've noticed this game once, added to wish list and bought it the same day it was released. It's a short game, for around 3-4 hours, but it's totally worth trying it. If you are into hacking and/or solving problems, finding information and coming up with answers, this is a perfect game for that.
This game might actually be peak fiction, buy it now.

Excellent setting and tone, great writing, great music, and the puzzles were always engaging without becoming frustrating. I was impressed by the variety of unique puzzles they fit into this game, given the constraints around setting. While 14 dollars might sound pricey given it's only around 3 hours long, I feel it is worth it because of how well made and entertaining this was. If you enjoyed Hypnospace outlaw or other similar games, or enjoy the x files, I think you'll enjoy this.

Very mild spoiler relating to a specific event:
[spoiler] I also really enjoyed the more realistic depiction of different aspects of cyber operations & defense. The SQL injection part was fun; I almost wish there was a game like this that doubled as an introduction to pen testing. Would be really fun I think. [/spoiler]

Intuitive and a thriller in it's own regard! The music sets the mood and wow, the interface is great! You just need a little patience and logical thinking with the puzzles, don't rush to quick to press that '?' help button XD The story was great, the twists and turns, the revaltions were amazing! I just wish it was longer!!! I need to find out more! I'm also sad that there weren't multiple endings!! Trust! GET THE GAME!

I was enjoying this game... right until the last mission. Spoiler-free explanation: Feels like a waste of time.

Spoilers ahead.




The game felt incomplete. The ending feels like a Diabolus ex Machina, which instead of leaving me feeling intruiged, left me disappointed. Doesn't feel like the time I spent in the story even mattered.
I get that the Organization is extremely powerful, but that does not translate well -- to me at least -- as an ending to a game. The one trope I absolutely hate is the "All For Nothing" trope, and unfortunately this is the exact embodiement of it.
This would work for a much longer game as a Prologue. This doesn't work as a game in and of itself.
Shame. I was looking forward to this one.

reviews.review: One of the best games in the captive desktop genre of games, honestly I really loved the game and hope to see more int the future!

I'm not sure how I feel about this on the fence yeah its good in some aspects bad in others. but the bad out weigh the good just being a boring point and click with many aspects that just say look through all files till you find something. give it a try if you want but its a coin flip of a game.

The game is a fun story, in a "operate a computer" setting. You can feel a bit hacker-y and competent. Visuals and Audio are appealing and immersive. The game is voiced for all characters that require being heard (there are some pure-chat-interactions).

The story itself if obviously the heart of the game. It doesnt get bogged down in the whos, whats and logistics of things. Some plot points seem predictable, but there are some rather cool reveals.

If you ever thought you wanted to jump into the deep end about the "what could be" of US-Government Law Enforcement, this will be a fun ride. 

The game is quite short, taking me about 3.5 hours to complete with repeating a certain part twice (about 20 extra minutes). 

The game having this length is POSITIVE. It doesnt overstay its welcome, features introduced are unique in their own way and operate smoothly. 

Give this game a try, I think this developer should try his hands at another game of this type.
The perfect detective game. Even though it ended beautifully, wished there was more game play.
super fun to play, a success!

Amazing game that the devs clearly put alot of work into.  One critique, you should have called it "Real stories of the FBI" since it's probably closer to what they really do then some fictional story.  Well done and I'd love to see some follow-up DLC.

Sound design is great and voice acting is also really good.

shorter than I thought it may be, but a very good story. curious to see if we get a sequel or DLC down the line - there are some mechanics i would like to have more opportunities to use.

Fun and interesting, The Operator brings the vibes of conspiracy and mystery that is very much along the lines of X-Files. The puzzles are interesting and varied, and all hook together into the narrative. 

Its not a long game by any means, but the price reflects it. 

I'd recommend this for any fans of detective style games.

It's worth playing as it isn't very long. The gameplay concept and execution are really good. The voice acting is pretty decent and makes the visual novel style content engaging to consume in addition to the gameplay mechanics. They have some pretty good tricks to flesh out the experience and make it feel more "real" while still managing to keeping the game very lo-fi...

I think it had a lot more potential than it tapped into. A very common criticism will be linearity and lack of player choice or replayability. There are a few moments where you can alter the outcome of an event that feels like it should have a more meaningful impact on the story, but the impact on the overall narrative is actually very little.  I also feel they were very close to allowing you to play the detective by doing your own extracurricular investigating, but then they sort of throw that out by having a character just be like "I bet you didn't notice THIS!" It's like... actually I did notice it and I wanted to have my moment of feeling like a genius. I think this is something that the Ace Attorney games do a little better.... while still railroading you into a very specific solution and solution path, they at least make you feel like you figured things out and make it feel rewarding. I think this game could have done at least more of that if not going as far as to actually add in more optional discovery and unprompted use of the information you gathered.

I'll also say that while this is a pretty good standalone narrative game concept, it feels like something I'd like to see integrated into a bigger game that doesn't play exclusively like this.

[h1] OPEN SPOILERS AT OWN RISK [/h1]

Well worth the price of admission. 

The dialogue can be a little cheesy at times and [spoiler] the ending might not be loved by everyone [/spoiler] but I thoroughly enjoyed it. 

The gameplay flowed well and there was only one point at which I needed to ask for help and felt the answer a little iffy [spoiler] I should be able to recognize my own apartment damn it! [/spoiler] but the rest were perfect, which is very hard to do in a puzzle game.

Also, using a carousel of user supplied pictures for the characters is a really neat idea and I commend the ingenuity. 

Definitely wouldn’t be opposed to more stories in this universe.

I really enjoyed playing the game and I definitely recommend it.

Our immersion in the game as a new FDI Operator is brilliant. Without forgetting the visual experience, its sounds, its puzzles and its narration
love this game!

A great game! The "X-files" mood and aesthetics fit perfectly with the investigation and hacking mechanics. The story is intense. The UI is cristal clear. The sound design is spot-on and the music is awesome. And it's worth mentioning, you can play it in one sitting of about 3-4h. Great job to all! :)

I love everything about it. The little nuances when choosing certain dialog options, the reactions etc. just feels right. Gameplay is so much better than other games in that genre.

10/10 ♥

Refunded. Got the feeling as I was playing that I was being railroaded and checking the steam discussions seems to indicate that my instincts were correct with only one supposed cliffhanger ending.

You don't get to make any meaningful choices in the game, the game even goes so far as to overtly override your choices as if to insult you.

I don't really care for the overarching spooky aliens government conspiracy storyline, I just want a regular game where I help field agents solve cases. I'm not sure why that's so hard to achieve.

Likes: 
- The gameplay is fun ... it's a detective game based on a computer with a compelling storyline (you almost feel like you are a part of CSI)
- The storyline keeps you playing ... you want to know what happens next

Dislikes:
- The parts in between gameplay where "the operator" isn't behind his computer are tedious and you really aren't looking at anything except for some blurry outlines of lighting ... you're basically just staring at your screen for a few minutes with some background noise

Overall the game is really well crafted and I applaud the whole team for all the work they put into it. The storyline is truly engaging. I couldn't close the game before knowing what happened at the end.

I absolutely love The Operator! The gameplay is engaging, the graphics are stunning, and the storyline kept me hooked from start to finish. The strategic elements are well-balanced, and every mission feels rewarding. The only thing I would love to see added is an endless mode. However, the creators have mentioned that it's unlikely to be added due to the game being heavily storyline-based. Despite this, the game is still fantastic and highly recommended!
As a actual FDA agent in real life, this is very much exactly what we do but with drugs. Excellent Game.
i blew up agent pendall 4 times 🤑🤑

Firstly, I'd like to preface my review, by saying if you are interested in this game. Do not watch a play through of it, try the demo, see if your engaged and then buy the game. This review is spoiler free.

A lovely crafted indie detective thriller, with a fantastic narrative story provided me with a very enjoyable and gripping 3/4 hours of game play on my first play through. The game has been painstakingly crafted down to every individual element, and it really shows, but this love creates a gripping, edge of your seat experience which will make you truly engage with every character and feel every emotion in a short space of time. The time setting is fantastic, blending a feel of early 2000 technology, with modern software and interface feel. When the game says use headphones, I usually disagree. But this is one of the rare examples which playing with headphones or a decent speaker set-up takes this from a game to a true experience.

The game has got an excellent blend of mixed media, cinematic and a truly atmospheric score that intertwines with the narrative in a beautiful way to create this experience. Throughout the game it makes you constantly think, am I making the right choices, is this how I solve this puzzle, and gives you everything you need to figure these out in a well executed manner without holding your hand too much. Even the achievements have been carefully thought out to provide you just enough information that your inquisitive brain wants to fully unravel and unlock each one.

Do I wish the game was longer? Yes. Am I disappointing by this? No, I loved every second of my playtime and strongly look forward to what the developer and his talented contributors bring next. Would I consider buying a future DLC expansion? Easily, this has been the most engaged with a game I've been for a very long time, and I would love to see what the developer brings to the operative universe next. 

This game is truly, one of those rare indie gems, that brings the passion and story into an over saturated gaming market, and really makes you wish more development companies (Especially AAA) had the same mentality and craft.
Short, and very sweet

I absolutely loved the game. I was so engaged throughout the whole session. I kept wanting to know what will happen next. It’s definitely worth the money. Wish we can see more of this in the future 🙏🏻. 

Please recommend me similar games

I'm frankly astonished by the reviews...completed the whole game in less than two hours and feel like I was robbed of £11. 

Was it fun? Yeah, I guess, but very, very linear and just lots of systematic clicking.

RIDICULOUSLY short and with a wholly unsatisfying storyline ending all round that I'll be sure not to spoil, but that is both predictable, yet entirely short of explanation. Just as you think the game and story is about to really get going...the game ends with little to no answers.

I'm utterly bemused that THIS is the final released version of the game.

I think it's important to go into this game with the proper expectations.

This is not a "choices matter" game when it comes to narration, and the puzzle solving is also pretty minimal when it comes to interactivity. There are a few hidden things you can find but for the most part you're mainly going to be going through the motions and left-clicking your way through the story in around 3 hours.

As it is, I'd say the game is more of an interactive visual novel, and maybe a proof of concept of something that could be done using these bones as a framework for a bigger project where actions and choices have consequences down the line, and where puzzles eventually become less hand-holdy or trivial as you progress through a longer story.

This is still nice as an atmospheric story-driven game with a good ambiance that will keep you entertained for an evening, and hopefully if the game does well enough, we could eventually see a more fully-realized version of what this game appears to want to do, but can't due to its relatively small scope.
A short but incredible game with a lot of attention to details. The story, the music and the voice acting are top notch. Worth every single penny.

Daily Game Review
Day 9

I don't know what I just experienced, but it probably will be one of the games that will randomly pop up back into my head every now and then.
The premise of the story is nothing new, you are a new operator at a police force and have to help people remotely, even some story strings are kinda cliche, but that doesn't mean it's badly written. Because I may be damned is the execution well done. While some plottwists are predictable, some are also coming out of nowhere, and are executed very well. Combine this with the developers display of their usage of sound, they just hit that much harder. The visuals of the game are also quite nice and well done, they just fit the atmosphere, especially the sequences between scenes, they really have that very special melancholic feeling for them going, of which I can only name a handful of titles that pull them off.

I really recommend this game as an experience to make, and who knows, maybe I won't be the only one who now has a worm called "The Operator" infiltrating their brain.

Have you been watching the Blacklist and wondered what it would be like to sit there at a desk all day?
Look no further, for 'The Operator' is here!!

On a more serious note though(BOOO, we want funny review).
This is a strong story driven mystery/conspiracy puzzle solving game.
For me it felt really rewarding solving the cases and the 'reward' of more information every time you solve something.
The great way of storytelling and keeping you on edge kept me hooked from the beginning.
Definitely worth the price if you're asking me!
10/10: would erase my memory to play again ;)

Strong enjoyable narrative and the voice acting I thought was very good! I really enjoyed that each puzzle was interesting, though I do wish it was longer or that we got to use some of the tools more.

I would be interested if there are plans for additional installments or chapters, it feels like a game that could have a fun overarching narrative.

I didn't mind paying the full cost because I def wanted to support the devs, but I would understand if people thought it's too high for a 3-5 hour game. That said, I would still recommend it and hope they make more of them!

The game was very short and i loved every moment. very high tense moments just wish there was more gameplay. finished it very shortly its one of the shortest and interesting games I've ever played. i hope the add more or perhaps a dlc maybe
amazing story, what a game

A very neat investigation game set in a US Federal police bureau. The story is compelling, the 90's atmosphere is great, the sound design is awesome and the user Interface really serves the atmosphere and narration. The difficulty level is just right, the puzzles are fun, the whole game goes by without getting bored one second. A very nice gem, highly recommended.

After playing Orwell and Stories Untold, I have been waiting for a new game in the same genre. And I was not disappointed!

The theme, the music, the UI, the writing, the investigations: everything's is so well designed so you can really fill the shoes of an Operator: you're behind your computer, resolving mysterious cases and you can feel the pressure!

My only disappointment is that I want MORE!
Thank you so much, loved every seconds of it :)

Surprisingly good game but I wish it was a little longer. The story was well written and the puzzles were witty. In a way, this game reminded me of the Orwell games that came out a few years back. Really did feel like you were playing an information analyst for the FBI. Despite the game being completed in less than 4 hours, it is well worth a play.

Nice game, very immersive.
Merci!!
